clue.text: Old man provides me with so sound an uplift

parts.note: taken as written
so, in the sense of in this way

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting a word up makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: sound as in healthy

explanation.surface: An elderly man offers to give someone a hearty boost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' and 'an' are part of the stringing: me, with so, and a sound one turned upside down make METHUSELAH.
explanation.definitionFit: Methuselah is the Bible's longest-lived patriarch, so his name stands for any very aged fellow.

clue.text: Vegetable only half-cooked?

parts.note: surface reading: some greens taken off the heat too soon
setter's reading: this legume is literally divided into halves, nothing to do with cooking

explanation.surface: A cook serves greens that are barely done.
explanation.walkthrough: The dried pea is split in two, so it is 'half' a vegetable before it ever sees a pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Split peas are dried peas divided along their seam, a pulse used in soups and dal.

clue.text: Remain perfectly still and go cold all over

definitions.meaning: second meaning: become chilled or turn to ice

explanation.surface: Someone stands motionless in terror, chilled to the bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both stopping all motion, as a startled animal does, and being chilled to icy temperatures.

clue.text: Objects and doesn't go on

definitions.meaning: first meaning: aims or purposes, as in means and ...

explanation.surface: Someone protests and then refuses to continue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objects' reads as a verb, to protest, but it is the plural noun meaning goals.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means goals or purposes; as a verb it means comes to a finish or stops.

clue.text: Located the cause of the trouble and criticised

definitions.text: Located the cause of the trouble
definitions.meaning: first meaning: tracked down the defect, as an engineer might

explanation.surface: A mechanic diagnoses the problem and then grumbles about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, discovering a defect; idiomatically, carping or complaining about someone's shortcomings.

clue.text: Company with deficit states huge figure

parts.note: standard abbreviation for company
a shortfall of money
the United States

explanation.surface: A firm in the red announces an enormous number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'States' reads as the verb announces, but it supplies the abbreviation for America.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colossus of Rhodes was a giant statue, so the word names any gigantic statue or towering person.

clue.text: Wiseacre makes a witticism, spoken in French

parts.note: a play on words
the French past participle of dire, to say

explanation.surface: A know-all cracks a joke in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiseacre is someone who claims expertise; a pundit is a self-styled expert who pronounces opinions.

clue.text: Fed up youngsters beginning to flout authority

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the word from the bottom

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the initial of the word youngsters

explanation.surface: Teenagers who are fed up start to rebel against their elders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' looks like the idiom for annoyed, but it is a word plus its turnaround signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist or openly disobey those in charge is a standard sense of the verb.

clue.text: Language that provides neat prose

indicators.note: the language provides, or makes out of, these letters by laying them out afresh

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Praise for a tongue that lends itself to tidy writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Provides' is an unusually gentle signal: the language is what the letters of the last two words make.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is the constructed international tongue devised by Zamenhof in the 1880s.

clue.text: Round safety devise that's practicable

parts.note: the letter shaped like a circle
a fuse protects a circuit; the source spells device as devise

explanation.surface: A circular safety gadget that works in practice.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'devise' is a slip for device, the gadget that cuts the current.
explanation.definitionFit: Something serviceable or usable can be put to good work, which is what this phrase says.

clue.text: She is expected to succeed

parts.note: surface reading: a woman tipped for success in her career
setter's reading: to succeed is to follow on, taking over an estate from a parent

explanation.walkthrough: Succeed means achieve, but here it means come next and inherit.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman due to inherit property or a title is the one in line to follow its present holder.

clue.text: Small number performing for 24 hours — 12 in fact

parts.note: abbreviation for number, and short
a performer is on stage
a full day

explanation.surface: A modest group puts on a show around the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: '12 in fact' is the definition: twelve o'clock in the middle of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is twelve o'clock, the time named by this slightly old-fashioned word for midday.

clue.text: Musician wanted a meal right away

indicators.note: sent away means removed, so the abbreviation for right goes

parts.note: the evening meal
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A performer is hungry and wants feeding immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right away' looks like immediately, but it splits into the letter R and its removal. Franz von Suppé was an Austrian composer of operettas such as Light Cavalry.
explanation.definitionFit: Suppé was a nineteenth-century Austrian composer, so he fits the general label of a music maker.

clue.text: What a taxi driver may do? That's a lot of rubbish!

definitions.text: What a taxi driver may do?
definitions.meaning: first meaning: turn down a gratuity, read as a verb and noun
second meaning: a dump where garbage piles up

explanation.surface: A cabbie waves away the extra money, and someone scoffs at the notion.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase, it is declining a gratuity; read as a compound noun, it is a British name for a rubbish dump.
explanation.definitionFit: A municipal dump in Britain is called this; a cabbie might also decline extra money offered.

clue.text: Lacking respect, notwithstanding

definitions.meaning: first meaning: without esteem, read as a word plus -less
second meaning: in spite of everything

explanation.surface: Someone behaves rudely, whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense takes the word literally, as having no esteem for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means despite or anyway; literally split, it describes a person without esteem for others.

clue.text: Dostoevsky's partner in crime

parts.note: surface reading: an accomplice of the Russian writer in some misdeed
setter's reading: the second word in the title of his novel that begins with Crime

explanation.walkthrough: Dostoevsky's novel is Crime and ..., so the word paired with Crime in that title is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: The novel's title joins Crime with its consequence, the penalty a wrongdoer receives.

clue.text: Who'll go first?

parts.note: surface reading: asking which person takes the opening turn
setter's reading: the query itself is about leading, so it is a query that leads

explanation.walkthrough: The query is about who will lead, making it literally a question about leading; in court the phrase means one that prompts the desired reply.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, a query worded to steer the witness toward a particular reply is given this name.

clue.text: Uniformed footmen

parts.note: surface reading: liveried servants in a grand house
setter's reading: men who go on foot, wearing army kit

explanation.walkthrough: Footmen are household servants in livery, but here they are simply soldiers who march.
explanation.definitionFit: Foot soldiers in an army make up this branch, as distinct from cavalry or artillery.

clue.text: Personal hint

definitions.meaning: first meaning: private or close, an adjective
second meaning: suggest indirectly, a verb with a different stress

explanation.walkthrough: The adjective and verb are spelt alike but said differently; the verb is stressed on its last syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means private or close; as a verb it means to suggest something without saying it outright.

clue.text: Precipitate way the staff leave school assembly?

parts.note: surface reading: hasty or rash, a word that also means hurl down

parts.words: way the staff leave school assembly?
parts.note: setter's reading: the principal teacher exits before the others

explanation.surface: Teachers dash out of a morning gathering in a rush.
explanation.walkthrough: At assembly the head teacher leaves before everyone else, so the order of exit puts the head in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Plunging forward with the skull leading means acting rashly or with reckless haste.

clue.text: Like to run when so inclined

parts.note: like in the sense of in the manner of
to run with long easy strides

explanation.surface: A jogger only goes out for a run when in the mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So inclined' looks like willing, but it means tilted, at an angle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tilted or on a slant is at an angle, which is what this adjective and adverb describe.

clue.text: Barrels used for target practice

definitions.meaning: first meaning: large casks for beer or water
second meaning: a range of mounds behind shooting targets

explanation.surface: Some casks are set up for shooters to aim at.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means large casks for liquid, and also the earth banks or range used by archers and riflemen.

clue.text: Miscalculate and tip a pound note

parts.note: British slang for a bribe or a sly payment, and also to toss
L, from Latin libra, is the pound sign
a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone gets their sums wrong and hands over a banknote as a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound note' looks like a banknote, but the words split into two single letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To botch something, such as a sum, is to make a clumsy mess of it, close to getting it wrong.

clue.text: Officer cut off in pass

indicators.note: in says one word sits within another

parts.note: a mountain pass
isolated or solitary

explanation.surface: A military man is stranded in a mountain gap.
explanation.walkthrough: A col is a low gap between two peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a senior commissioned rank in the army, just below brigadier.

clue.text: Common complaint of many of advanced years

parts.note: the Roman numeral for a hundred, standing for many
aged

explanation.surface: An ailment that bothers lots of elderly people.
explanation.definitionFit: The everyday viral infection of nose and throat is the commonest minor illness of all.

clue.text: Short dress on mother, to say the least

parts.note: a very short skirt or dress
British informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A short frock on someone's mum is, putting it mildly, a surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To say the least' looks like an aside, but it defines the smallest possible amount.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'at the very least' points to the lowest acceptable amount or lower limit.

clue.text: It may flow and sound like the sea

indicators.note: sound like tells us to go by how the word is said, not spelt

parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the open sea

explanation.surface: Something that runs like water and echoes the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It may flow' fits a stream, but it describes a horse's or lion's long neck hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's or lion's long neck hair is often described as flowing in the wind.

clue.text: Outcast reflects the way people treat him

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the word is read back to front

parts.note: people push him away

explanation.surface: A shunned man mirrors how others behave toward him.
explanation.walkthrough: People drive away a sufferer of leprosy, and that verb read backwards is the person.
explanation.definitionFit: Lepers were historically shunned and banished, so the word means anyone rejected by society.

clue.text: Going out, Nigel's not the only one in a suit

definitions.text: the only one in a suit

indicators.note: going out suggests letters straying from their places and regrouping

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Nigel stays in while the others head out, the lone one in a business suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' is a card suit, not clothing: a hand holding just one card of that suit.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, holding just one card of a suit in a dealt hand is called this.
